findings.detail: Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2A-SAME-HEIGHT-05 (and Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2A-PROJECTILE-APEX-03) mount the single EVENT-CLOCK scene 'Requested event: the stone reaches the ground', a horizontal launch from a cliff with event condition Δy = −h, both pre-attempt (V0) and post-attempt (V0–V3). Item 05 is a same-height landing (correct event Δy = 0, non-zero root t = 2u_y/g = 4 s); item 03 is the apex (correct event v_y = 0, t = u_y/g = 2 s). The bound figure for 05 draws exactly the wrong event this item's failure signal warns about. Each item needs a scene instance of its own event: apex marker with v_y = 0 and v_x = 12 m/s for 03; level launch/landing with Δy = 0 for 05.

The construction unit that teaches 'v_y = 0 at the apex, Δy = 0 at a return to launch height' (worked anchor: level ground, u = (6, 15) m/s, apex 1.5 s / 11.25 m, landing 3 s / 18 m) stages the cliff figure whose only event is ground impact below launch (Δy = −h). No stage shows an apex or a same-height event, so the representation contradicts the decision it is meant to carry. The same figure is reused unchanged for CU-PHY-KIN-PROJECTILE-MODEL-3, where the launch has u_y = 20 m/s upward but the figure shows a horizontal launch (u_x only).

Core1B 'Attempt' prints elicitation.attempt.produces as the task: 'A two-column x/y setup with one shared t.' (likewise 'Two correct component constant-acceleration equations using one t.' and 'A model declaration and component-equation setup for a horizontal or oblique projectile.' for the other two microtopics). These describe the expected output; the learner is given no situation to set up, so there is nothing concrete to attempt before the reconstruction opens. Each microtopic needs a concrete attempt prompt (e.g. 'x(t) = 5t, y(t) = 12 − 2t²: write both component columns and read the position at t = 2 s'), with 'produces' kept as the rubric.

Three of the five Core2B transfer tasks restate items the learner has already answered with the answer shown: 02 (a_x = 2, a_y = 3t: constant-a exact only on x) is the Core1B boundary test of MIC-PHY-KIN-2D-CONSTANT-ACCELERATION; Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-PROJECTILE-VALIDITY-04 (retained horizontal thrust: reject a_x = 0) is the Core1B boundary test of MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJECTILE-MODEL and panel B of the Core1A figure; Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-SAME-HEIGHT-VELOCITY-05 (same height: v_x equal, v_y equal and opposite, speed equal, velocity different) is the Core1A diagnose/repair pair of CU-PHY-KIN-PROJECTILE-MODEL-2 word for word. The demand does not change for these three; only 01 (verbal directions to signed components) and 03 (unequal-height landing, t = 3 s, 30 m) are genuine transfers.

Hint rung 4 (purpose CONNECT, from scaffolds[1]) does not climb past rung 3 in items 01–04: 01 'Label the time beside each evaluated component' repeats rung 2; Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2A-CONSTANT-ACCEL-02 rung 4 restates rung 3; Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2A-PROJECTILE-APEX-03 rung 4 'decide which velocity component changes sign' steps back from rung 3 'set only v_y to zero, solve'; Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2A-HORIZONTAL-LAUNCH-04 rung 4 'name the physical condition that says the stone has reached the ground' steps back to orientation. Only item 05 (root selection) climbs. No rung gives the answer early (checked on all five).

The answer 0.5 s is correct but step 3 of the working does not derive it ('no stated vertical impulse … The source configuration yields the same vertical fall time'), and step 2 assumes what it should prove (H = ½g(0.5)² presumes zero initial vertical speed). Correct chain: u_x = u_y = 5 m/s, apex at 0.5 s, H = u_y²/2g = 1.25 m; a fragment falling from 1.25 m in 0.5 s started from rest; momentum at the apex (M·5 horizontal, 0 vertical) gives the other fragment (10, 0) m/s; with zero vertical velocity from 1.25 m it lands after t = √(2H/g) = 0.5 s (and at x = 2.5 + 5 = 7.5 m, as Q6 states).

CU-PHY-KIN-2D-CONSTANT-ACCELERATION-1 reuses the CU-PHY-KIN-2D-INDEPENDENT-COMPONENTS-1 shared-clock figure unchanged (v_x constant, v_y falling from 0). Its decision is 'check on each axis that its acceleration component is constant', but no stage shows a_x, a_y or a per-axis constancy check, and the worked anchor (u = (4, 6), a = (0, −2), t = 6 s, 24 m) has v_y starting positive, not at 0. Core1 also mounts this same figure for all three microtopics, including the projectile-model one, which has its own REP-KIN-2D-PROJECTILE-MODEL.

The safe pre-attempt figure shows a horizontal launch (u_x arrow only) from a cliff, but the task launches with u_y = +10 m/s upward from 15 m; the drawn trajectory never rises. Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-SAME-HEIGHT-VELOCITY-05 (two equal-height points on one arc) is given the same cliff/ground-impact scene. Figures must show this item's launch (u = (10, 10) m/s, ground 15 m below) and, for 05, two marked equal-height points.

Every page's h1, title and breadcrumb show 'Owner-approved ExamSIDE question-demand slice for plane motion, now semantically', which is scope_summary truncated mid-sentence and is internal provenance language. The learner-facing title should be the bucket title 'Two-dimensional kinematics and projectile model'.

The restatement drops what the 10 m is measured from ('a pebble is launched at 45 degrees from a point 10 m away'). The working needs it to be 10 m from the fixed end of the spring (block at 5.1 m, then 5.0 m after 1 s, so the pebble covers 5 m). Say '10 m from the wall to which the spring is fixed, toward the block'. Similarly PYQ-PHY-JEEADV-2023-P1-Q01 option (B) uses z-hat without stating that ẑ points vertically up.

The failure signal ('time from 20/15 ≈ 1.33 s, range 20 m') is not a route learners take; the common wrong routes here are a sign slip (+20 = 5t², then taking √ of a negative, or t = √(h/g) = 1.41 s from dropping the ½) or applying the same-height formula 2u_y/g = 0. Also bound_ref is REP-KIN-2D-SHARED-CLOCK while initial_ref is the event figure, so the post-attempt review shows a different, generic scene.
Option labels are doubled: '(a) (A) sqrt(50) m/s (b) (B) …' (also PYQ-PHY-JEEADV-2023-P1-Q01 and PYQ-PHY-JEEADV-2026-P1-Q06). Print the source label once.

The 'Lineage check' block prints the 'What stayed valid' and 'What changed' sentences again, verbatim, directly below them. It adds no check. The safe pre-attempt support sentence is also identical on all five tasks ('Commit to a model or representation and your first relation before opening support.').

Gating holds: in Chromium, clicking or pressing Enter/Space on every gated summary without an attempt left it closed, and window.find did not expand it. But the unlock accepts any 3 non-space characters ('abc'), and the page search matches text inside locked answers, so typing an answer value (e.g. '170') filters to the item that contains it.
